Content will include a new free map and the option to buy new Michael skins, new Civilian characters, and a very special Halloween Costume pack!

Now that players have had their hands on Michael Myers as he appeared in the film that started it all, “John Carpenter’s Halloween,” we are excited to share that we have partnered with Trancas International Films, Inc., and MIRAMAX to license new versions of Michael.

On October 27, 2026, players can purchase the version of Michael from “Halloween 5: The Revenge of Michael Myers,” and the version of Michael from “Halloween 2018,” which mask design is being supervised by Academy Award winner Christopher Nelson, who sculpted the mask for the recent and highly successful trilogy of “Halloween 2018,” “Halloween Kills,” and “Halloween Ends.”
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748220/9a70aa8028021a9e6bd27f13201c6e64ea721c3b.jpg"]

In addition, a new map will be added for all players who purchased the game, inspired by the settings of “Halloween 5” – The Tower Farm Map – where worn country roads meet at the center of a small, quaint farming community just outside of Haddonfield. A lit filling station anchors the new map, providing Civilians a reference point as they scramble across wide roads and through cornfields. While the map’s open nature helps with navigation, it also creates a no-man’s land where Civilians can become easy prey. Hide in roadside ditches to stay out of sight, then pray for the perfect moment for a harrowing sprint to safety.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748220/60b75161b5798c78ef674363d1a41b00ee8ec8a8.jpg"]

Farmhouses replace suburban homes, shifting the feel and flow of 1v4 multiplayer matches. Farm equipment, hay bales, and overgrown brush turn every yard into a twisted playground for Michael Myers to attack. Barns, sheds, and houses give Civilians a chance to escape, catch their breath, and have a chance at evading the Boogeyman.

[p align="start"]A harvest festival, trailer park, and pumpkin-filled gardens bring the new map to autumnal life, lit by the last light of a setting sun. A basement chase or a sprint through the pumpkin patch can go either way: seek new hiding spots and exits while Michael finds fresh ways to stalk his prey.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748220/b05195b92d2360bdb6e9dda3c3449d1f040859b5.jpg"]

In addition to the new Tower Farm map and two Michael Myers skins, we will also be introducing two new Civilians, a very special Halloween costume pack, and more in the first of a series of post-launch content updates for Halloween: The Game that will be carried out across the first year.

[p align="start"]“1978 was only the beginning,” said Jared Gerritzen, Chief Creative Officer, IllFonic. “With the Tower Farm map, we take the terror of that first event in Haddonfield into somewhere wide open, where there’s nowhere to hide except in the dark – where Michael Myers truly comes to life.”

Today, we are incredibly excited to release our first Quality of Life update for Halloween: The Game. Patch 1.1.0 was built around community feedback and delivering on our promises of improving the overall experience for our players. This update is bursting with a huge number of bug and crash fixes, optimization enhancements, meaningful balance changes, gameplay improvements, and more!

While we are thrilled about our first major content drop coming later this month, addressing the issues impacting our current players remains a key priority for the team. Patch 1.1.0 demonstrates our commitments to Halloween: The Game and our amazing community. Thanks so much for playing!
Crash Fixes and Optimization

Our first Quality of Life update features a variety of crash fixes and refinements to performance and optimization. We are continuing to monitor opportunities for additional performance gains with future updates, but players should notice improvements across all platforms with 1.1.0.
Added support for DLSS-G
Shaders now precompile at startup on PC
Improved performance when using DLSS, FSR and XeSS
Improved CPU and GPU performance across all maps
Improved Xbox Series S stability
Fixed several crashes affecting players using specific AMD hardware
Fixed several crashes that occurred during Story Mode
Fixed several crashes that occurred during Execution cinematics
Fixed crashes that could occur when using Quick Resume on Xbox Series X|S
Added a “Graphic Card Not Supported” message for users on hardware below minimum specs
Various other crash fixes

Our team has been closely monitoring match pacing as players have become more familiar with the core gameplay loop of Halloween: The Game. Today’s update includes a series of focused adjustments designed to minimize objective rushing and slow down overall match pacing for both Michael and Civilian players. We’re discussing additional tuning opportunities in this regard, but the following changes are designed to increase tension and encourage deeper strategy.

In many instances, the Storm Cellar Escapes were simply too reliable, which led players to prioritize these escape routes over others. In an effort to adjust early match pacing we are making Storm Cellars more challenging to open while also introducing some adjustments to Escape Discovery Distance.
Discovery Distance for Escapes now scales with match time, increasing as matches progress
Reduced the amount of Bolt Cutters, Gas Cans, and Escape Keys that spawn in a match
Made adjustments to Escape Item spawn locations to reduce instances where multiple may appear in close proximity
Reduced the Storm Cellar Escape Capacity
Reduced the Gate Escape Capacity
Increased the amount of Fuses that spawn in a match
Increased the minimum amount of Escape Blockers that may appear on Storm Cellars
Increased the amount of time required to Clear Overgrowth

To further address issues regarding rapid match pacing, we are also tweaking the amount of Bloodthirst required to gain Bloodthirst levels as Michael. Stalking and performing Executions will now feel far more impactful to overall Bloodthirst gains compared to simply racking up basic kills as fast as possible.
Increased Bloodthirst required for each Bloodthirst level
Increased Bloodthirst gained from Stalking and Executions
Increased Bloodthirst gained from a successful Grabs and attacks
Reduced Shape Jump visibility range at Bloodthirst levels 1 and below
Reduced Shape Jump movement speed at Bloodthirst levels 2 and below
Increased Shape Dash movement speed

Our team continues to monitor the dynamics of melee combat and various stunt interactions in Halloween: The Game. We want to ensure that melee combat feels reliable for both Michael and Civilians but we’ve also identified instances where Civilian players feel they don’t have the proper agency to counter incoming attacks. We’ve made further tuning to prevent instances where players are “locked” in repeated stun states.
Increased Civilian Stagger and Stumble cooldown from being hit by a melee attack
Increased the delay between the initial strike of attack combos for the Hatchet and Meat Cleaver to prevent players from repeatedly using the initial attack instead of continuing the combo
Reduced damage increase from Bloodthirst tier 2 and 3
Reduced attack speed increase from Bloodthirst tier 2 and 3
Reduced the duration of the slow applied when taking melee damage
Reduced the amount of slow applied when taking melee damage
Increased the effect of the brief movement speed buff gained when taking melee damage

Late game hunting can be challenging for Michael, especially when targets are inside Hiding Spots. We’ve made a few changes to Stalking to streamline the end of match experience and help Michael players clean up those remaining Residents and Special Targets.
Residents, Special Targets, and Civilians now become Stalked if they are in a Hiding Spot during the final 60 seconds of a match
Residents and Special Targets now become Stalked if Michael receives the objective to “Finish Off Haddonfield”
Stalked targets are now visible in Hiding Spots when either of the above criteria are met

Earlier this week, we rolled out Patch 1.0.3 for Halloween: The Game. While this update brought a variety of fixes and improvements to the experience, it also introduced a couple frustrating problems stemming from our changes to Grabs/Struggling.

As a special thanks to our community for enduring Michael’s inhumane grip strength and some lingering performance/optimization issues, especially on XBOX Series X|S, we are granting 10,000 Perk Points to all our current Halloween: The Game players.

Our original goal with Patch 1.0.3. was to allow Civilians increased opportunities to Struggle Free from Grabs at Stalk Tier 2 and below. Unfortunately, these changes in combination with other bug fixes associated with Grabs inadvertently caused it to become exponentially more difficult for a Civilian to Struggle Free from Michael at Bloodthirst Level 3 and caused Civilian players to sometimes take fall damage after successfully Struggling Free. We understand the irritation these issues produced and apologize for allowing them to slip through alongside our last update.
Fixed an issue where Bloodthirst Level 3 would cause Grabs to be way harder to escape from than intended
Fixed an issue where Struggling free from a grab while on uneven terrain would cause the Civilian to take fall damage

With Patch 1.0.4, our team has made strides in improving performance and stability on XBOX Series X|S. We’ve addressed a range of memory and GPU-related crashes, and adjusted Quality/Performance settings on both Series X and S.
Adjusted settings for Performance Mode on XBOX Series X to improve performance
Introduced a new singular graphics mode for XBOX Series S
In an effort to address stability issues, we have removed the Quality/Performance toggle on Series S
This Series S profile caps framerate at 30 FPS while improving overall texture quality and enabling hair physics during gameplay
Players have consistently reported performance problems when Loomis enters the match as a reinforcement character. Ironically, we identified a significant performance hit rooted in Loomis’ hair.
Fixed an issue where Loomis spawning in would cause players to experience a performance hit or, on lower-spec platforms, crash

This patch also includes fixes for a variety of crashes (such as crashing after completing a Story Mission or loading into a match) across all platforms. Crash fixes and optimization are ongoing priorities for our team and we plan to address additional issues with future updates.

It’s hard to believe that it’s already been two weeks since we welcomed players to Haddonfield with the official launch of Halloween: The Game. We are incredibly grateful to everyone who’s jumped into our asymmetrical horror sandbox so far, and our team continues to work tirelessly to refine the experience for our players.

As we discussed in our What’s Coming Next? post last week, thanks to your thoughtful feedback, our team has identified and prioritized a list of pain points to tackle. In today’s 1.0.3 patch, we are very excited to address many of these issues by introducing a host of bug and crash fixes, balance adjustments, and gameplay improvements.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748220/ddd152de5b6e2ac0cbb6a0ba927dd21515b6d927.png"]

As we continue to play, monitor, and gather feedback, we’ve identified some balance adjustments we felt were necessary for this patch. Many of these changes are being rolled out to minimize frustrating, overpowered, or unenjoyable situations. While we are happy to implement the following changes, we have also identified additional balance opportunities we plan to release with future updates. Your passionate feedback has been greatly beneficial to the team and we are eager to continue improving Halloween: The Game.
Civilian Melee Rebalance

We performed a Civilian-focused melee rebalance to eliminate easy one-shot Michael downs, especially when using Bob and Laurie or Perks that give a boost while Drunk. This also included buffing Michael’s Bloodthirst Damage Resistance to extend the duration of melee encounters. We want Civilians to be capable of fighting back against Michael, but we recognized that certain characters could inflict extremely high damage far too consistently.
Reduced effectiveness of Capability for Melee Damage at higher stat values
Increased effectiveness of Capability for Melee Damage at lower stat values
Reduced Fear Resistance granted by the Heavyweight trait
Reduced Melee Damage granted by the Heavyweight trait
Reduced effect of Civilian melee damage boost while Drunk
Increased Michael’s damage resistance across all Bloodthirst levels

While there were already mechanics in place to bolster Michael after he recovers from being Downed, we’re adding additional buffs in this patch to combat harassment and avoid instant follow-up downs. This, combined with the above melee rebalancing, addresses the ease in which these occurrences could happen and ensures Michael always has ample means of retaliation if he is being surrounded or consistently pressured by an aggressive squad.

Michael now gains a short duration buff after getting up from a Downed state. This buff grants Michael Stagger immunity and an increase in Damage Resistance, Melee Damage, and Melee Attack Speed for the duration of the buff.
Michael will also be empowered with increased Health Regeneration and Daze Resistance for a short period of time after getting up from a Downed state

To provide more time for players to react to incoming hits we are introducing a small damage reduction and a small increase to time in between all attack combos for Wood Axes and Pickaxes. We don’t want to discourage melee combat and would prefer to provide players additional opportunities to counter. Civilians should now have more time to shove during melee combos to interrupt Michael and experience increased cooldown time between stumbles. We are also adjusting the available quantities of certain weapon types on maps to increase their rarity and further incentivize exploration.
Reduced Combo Attack Speed for the Wood Axe and Pick-Axe
Reduced light and heavy Attack Damage for the Wood Axe and Pick-Axe
Lowered amount of heavy Melee Weapons, Rifles, and Shotguns spawns across all maps and locations
Increased the Stagger cooldowns for Civilians
Reduced overall Melee Weapon Durability

We are taking some steps to balance the value of Special Targets and Residents to ensure match scoring better represents the overall outcome and creates greater opportunities for mid-to-late game swings. We have lowered the score values for killing Special Targets, while increasing the score values for both saving and killing Residents. While we plan to improve Special Target spawning, tracking, and more with future updates, these changes will make every Resident, Civilian, and Special Target feel important to the final score.
Made adjustments to scoring to balance Michael’s priority on normal Residents vs Special Targets

We are continuing to monitor the balance of Grabs and Struggling. In previous patches, we made it easier for Civilians to struggle free from Grabs at lower Stalk Tiers. In today’s patch we have made adjustments to further reduce the difficulty of escaping Grabs. We also lowered the force caused by failed Grab attempts so Civilian players won't stumble as dramatically, allowing a better chance to slip away. Our team is having ongoing conversations about pocket knives and we plan to provide more substantial tuning in the future, but for now we have increased the pocket knife minigame difficulty to allow Michael players slightly more time to pull off Context Executions.
Reduced impact force from failed Grab attempts on the Civilian player
Civilians now have an easier time Struggling free from grabs at Stalk Tiers 0-2
Reduced effectiveness of Capability for Grab Struggle at higher stat values
Slight increase to the difficulty of the Pocket Knife break free minigame

We’ve adjusted the effectiveness of Athleticism for movement and sprint speeds to reduce the speed of high Athleticism Civilians while also increasing the speed of low Athleticism Civilians. We noticed that certain Civilians were far too fast in their running and sprint speeds.
Reduced effectiveness of Athleticism for movement and sprint speeds at higher stat values
Increased effectiveness of Athleticism for movement and sprint speeds at lower stat values

We understand that challenges and their associated rewards are extremely important to players. We have and will continue to address fundamental issues impacting challenge progression and tune challenge requirements. Our latest patch brings a handful of corrections to challenge tracking along with a sweeping balance pass on Progressive Challenge goals.
Players with progress exceeding the required goals for Progressive Challenges after our updates simply need to gain any progress toward that objective to complete the challenge.
The full list of Challenge adjustments can be found at the bottom of the Patch Notes

Since our Early Access launch, our team has been working hard to quickly address reported bugs, improve performance, evaluate game feedback, and refine the overall experience for players. We’ve already implemented various server-side adjustments, one hotfix, and our Day One Patch. With the release of 1.0.2, we are excited to deliver our second hotfix.

Today’s update tackles a wide range of issues affecting game performance and stability, player interactions, challenges, achievements, and Prestige, alongside numerous bug fixes and carefully considered balance adjustments. Thanks so much to everyone who’s jumped in and joined us in Haddonfield so far. We greatly appreciate all the feedback and remain committed to enriching the distinct horror sandbox of Halloween: The Game.
Crashes, Stability, and Interactions
Patch 1.0.2 introduces numerous crash fixes and stability improvements across all platforms. We are collecting community feedback and investigating further optimization opportunities.

Our team is aware of performance and stability issues disproportionately impacting Xbox Series S players. We are actively working to improve visual fidelity, overall performance, and memory-related crashes. Players can expect additional focused fixes and improvements with an upcoming patch.

We've made several fixes to issues that were impacting player interactions and interaction prompts disappearing. This is an ongoing process, and we will be continuously investigating issues of this nature. We appreciate any and all feedback related to player interactions
Fixed several issues that were causing certain items to not be obtainable due to collision issues
Fixed an issue where the interaction prompts could disappear after an NPC has moved the player out of position while the player in engaged in conversation
Fixed an issue where the interaction prompts could disappear after a Civilian was affected by any collision while Grabbed
Fixed an issue where the interaction prompts could disappear when the Fragile Hourglass was used on Michael while he is downed
Fixed an issue where the interaction prompts for certain Escapes would disappear after repairing the Escape Car

We understand the frustrations players have experienced when it comes to specific challenges, achievements, and our Prestige system not functioning as intended. Our team actively investigated many of the biggest pain points our community was facing and worked to quickly address many of them with 1.0.2. The fixes introduced today make obtaining singleplayer challenges far more consistent, though we’ve identified additional ways to improve in-game messaging and the overall player experience, which we aim to address in future updates.

Various progression blockers for Passive and Progressive Challenges have also been corrected, alongside a fix for the issue preventing players from properly engaging with our Prestige Challenges. Thanks for all your patience and understanding. We’ll continue monitoring any other potential problems with challenges.
Fixed an issue where certain challenges that required the player to escort Residents to an escape were not being tracked properly
Fixed an issue where certain challenges that required the player to survive a match were not being tracked properly
Fixed an issue where the Killer Passive Challenge “Weight of the Mask” was not being tracked properly
Fixed an issue where the Rachel Progressive Challenge “Superstitious Tools” was not tracking the properly based on the description
Fixed an issue where the Rachel Progressive Challenge “Ward Off Evil” was gaining additional progress
Fixed an issue where the Hatchet Progressive Challenge “Wheels Clipped” was not tracking properly
Fixed an issue where the Kitchen Knife Progressive Challenge “Edge of the Blade” was not tracking properly
Fixed an issue where the Prologue Challenge 6 was not being tracked properly
Fixed an issue for Chapter 2 Challenge 6 where certain executions would count the player as alerting someone
Fixed an issue for Chapter 4 Challenge 2 that would cause Lynda to immediately leave the bedroom after Bob has been killed
Fixed an issue for Chapter 5 Challenge 1 where the flashlights were required to be completely drained to complete the challenge
Fixed several issues that were causing the following achievements/trophies to not track properly
Purist
Close Quarters
No Friend Left Behind
Natural Observer
Stalker
Reenabled Prestige Challenges
Fixed an issue where an active Prestige Challenge was preventing players from entering matchmaking
UPDATE 9/11 5:15 PM PST

After today's patch, there was a brief period when Weapon Prestige Challenges weren't populating as intended, including challenge criteria without text. This issue should be resolved across all Prestige Challenges.
Please restart the game for these changes to take effect.
We are aware certain challenges contain unclear objectives. While these challenges are still completable, we understand it's currently difficult to identify the proper completion criteria.
We are constantly working to improve the user experience. Please continue to send us any feedback regarding challenges.

Our team has been incredibly excited to have more opportunities to hop online and play matches with the community following our official launch on Tuesday. It’s been rewarding watching players craft their own Perk Decks, construct their distinct Michael loadouts, and discover the layered systems of Halloween: The Game. For this patch, we wanted to make a few focused balance adjustments.

We’re continuing to carefully monitor gameplay balance between Michael and Civilians to ensure matches feel tense and satisfying for both sides. We are gathering community feedback, playtesting changes, and factoring in match data to make the best decisions focused on ironing out additional instances of imbalance. We greatly appreciate the passionate exploration and discovery that’s helping us further identify and address the most problematic encounters. Keep it coming!

Bloodthirst Tiers enable Michael to bolster his damage resistance, grab strength, melee damage, ability cooldowns, Shape Jump speed, and more to drastically increase his capabilities. We’ve made the following change to improve Michael’s early game effectiveness:
Increased Michael’s base damage resistance
Increased Michael’s Bloodthirst tier 1 and 2 damage resistance
The Lethal Pitch Perk was showing itself to be far too effective in its upper tiers. We’ll be carefully watching this perk and many others to identify further balance opportunities.
Lowered the effectiveness of tiers 2, 3, 4, and 5 of Lethal Pitch Perk

With Pocket Knives being equippable as a Starting Item for Civilians, we’ve made the decision to reduce the total number of Pocket Knives and Icepicks available on each map. We want these items to feel valuable to players and provide rare opportunities for clutch moments of survival. We’ll continue monitoring the quantity and placement of these items as well.
Reduced the amount of Grab Escape Items (such as the Pocket Knife) spawns across all maps and locations
Fixes an issue where the escape car could behave erratically while escaping
Fixed an issue where the Redeem button in the Redeem Code menu was not working properly when using a controller
Fixed an issue where the facial animations would sometimes not play correctly on certain characters
Fixed an issue where players would not obtain any XP when leaving the match as a Spectator
Fixed an issue where the Brimstone Fuse trait effect was being calculated incorrectly
Fixed an issue where the Loomis Reinforcements Perk Card was not working properly
Fixed an issue where Followers would close and lock doors on the player
Fixed an issue where players spawning in as the Police would sometimes be missing dialogue and VOIP facial animations
Fixed an issue where collisions could cause players in the vehicle to take several instances of additional damage
Fixed an issue where the limited promotional “Regal” Eyewear was missing for Rachel
Fixed an issue where it was possible to kill Michael while he is interacting with the Storm Cellar and Exit Gate
Made improvements to the knockback animations for Michael when colliding with a high speed vehicle
Fixed an issue preventing rain VFX from appearing correctly in Public Matches

The launch of Early Access for Halloween: The Game has been amazing so far and the team is so excited to finally be able to play the game with you all.

Today we are rolling out our first hotfix for Halloween: The Game. This patch is primarily aimed towards addressing several crashes that have been occurring as well as a small list of other issues that the team was able to implement with this hotfix.
We are currently working on a bigger patch that addresses many issues and concerns that are being reported from the playerbase.
We will continue monitoring conversations and bug reports from the community, and we greatly appreciate all your feedback.
Thank you for all your love and support. See you in Haddonfield!
Numerous Crash Fixes
Fixes to several challenges that were not tracking properly
Fixed an issue where Offline Play was affected by the login queueing system
Fixed an issue where the prompt to get up after being downed as Michael would sometimes not appear
Fixed an issue causing the game to render incorrectly on Xbox Series S in “Performance Mode” on certain displays
